text:
arjun: throwing this out for discussion: for internal inference RPCs do we make gRPC-streaming the canonical API and let the edge translate for browsers, or keep a JSON-first public shape and make grpc optional for services?

celia: gRPC-first seems cleaner for service-to-service. Streaming lets us avoid header/body chattiness for token streams and keeps backpressure semantics native.

matt: +1 on perf but concerned about edge complexity. Translating streams -> chunked JSON (SSE/chunked) at the gateway can be messy when we need to apply quotas & rate-limit per-token.

sofia: idea: standardize on a tiny "frame" envelope proto that every stream uses. Gateway maps frames 1:1 to JSON chunks. If we version envelope conservatively we can add fields without breaking clients.

arjun: can you sketch that frame?

sofia: something like: Frame { oneof { token_chunk, meta, control } }
token_chunk includes seq, payload(bytes or base64), maybe condensed token_count. meta carries sampling ids and trace hints. control carries eos/err. Gateway will honor seq for ordering.

celia: where do quotas live? Gateway or runtime? If gateway does optimistic checks and runtime enforces exact charging, we get fast-fail UX but accurate billing. Need to avoid double-charging race conditions.

matt: agreed. Gateway should perform capacity checks against a soft quota API (token budget cache) and mark requests as provisional. Runtime finalizes charges and emits an event if quota is exceeded. Console will reconcile provisional vs final.

arjun: rollout UX: prefer header-based canary (X-Infer-Mode: streaming) and route weight control from console. Also need a rollback trigger based on tail-latency delta and token error rate.

ingress-bot: canary started: edge-proxy v2026.03.22-stream -> 5% at 1743221030

sofia: telemetry: add a sampled span_id per-request inside meta so we can stitch gateway <-> runtime logs. Keep sampling rate configurable to avoid cardinality explosion. Also emit token_count per-chunk metric.

celia: protocol versioning: reserve a single field number for an opaque extras map so gateway can forward unknown fields to JSON clients without losing them. Document and test forward-compat.

matt: implementation detail: Envoy's gRPC-web has quirks for flow-control; I'd rather a small dedicated ingress filter for inference routes that preserves streaming semantics and attaches quota headers, rather than depending on generic gRPC-web.

arjun: ops note: if we add dedicated sidecar, we need a small playbook for upgrades (drain connections gracefully). Also add a health probe that checks per-stream stability not just route up.

sofia: tests: (1) perf microbenchmark: 10k concurrent short streams vs long streams, compare CPU/latency for sidecar vs envoy-transcode. (2) Quota race sim: concurrent provisional passes then runtime reject path.

celia: action items: sofiato write proto sketch and unknown-field forwarding spec (PR by Thu). matt to prototype sidecar filter and run perf baseline. I'll draft quota provisional API and reconciliation design. arjun will add header canary flag to console and a simple rollout card.

arjun: ok thanks. small ask: put a sample JSON mapping in the spec so web teams can try it without switching to gRPC-web.

matt: will do a minimal example mapping.

arjun: if no objections we'll start the canary expansion after PRs land next week. :white_check_mark:
